title: Philippines and Australia committed to sovereignty, maritime security
summary: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese aim to strengthen the partnership of the two countries to reinforce national sovereignty and enhance maritime…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese during their bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits. Photo from Presidential Communications Office

President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese aim to strengthen the partnership of the two countries to reinforce national sovereignty and enhance maritime security, the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) announced.
Marcos and Albanese also discussed strengthening the region’s ability to respond to emerging security challenges amid growing geopolitical uncertainties.

The two leaders reaffirmed their Strategic Partnership during their bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits set as the two countries mark 80 years of diplomatic relations.

"The two leaders committed to expand defense cooperation through a new Defence Cooperation Arrangement covering maritime security, cyber defense, joint military operations, and other priority areas, reaffirming their shared commitment to a peaceful, stable, and rules-based Indo-Pacific," the PCO reported. — BAP, GMA News
